The complete 1903 disc is streamed, not a digitally assembled excerpt. Its approximately two-minute duration is not the complete score. Comparison alignment excludes the shortened ending and music found only in Vetter’s complete reading.

The Commons transfer’s restoration and replay speed are not documented. Marston discusses pitch instability in these early discs, but its modern restoration is not the audio streamed here.

[1] [4]
Composition rights
Underlying piano composition is public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms Inferred, not documented

Grieg died in 1907. This does not establish rights in a modern edition.

[1] [3]
Recording rights
US public domain: sound recording first published in 1903 Documented

IMSLP’s recording entry names Gramophone & Typewriter No. 3800, 1903, matrix 2149F; Marston corroborates matrix, pianist and 2 May 1903 session. The recording’s pre-1926 publication, not Commons’ composition-only PD-old tag, is the basis. No non-commercial restriction appears in the inspected source entry.

[3] [4] [5]

Edvard Grieg, Wedding Day at Troldhaugen, Op. 65 No. 6; Edvard Grieg, piano. Paris, 2 May 1903; Gramophone & Typewriter matrix 2149F, published 1903. Abridged performance; transfer engineer unknown; via Wikimedia Commons. Sound recording: US public domain. Rights statement

  1. Wikimedia Commons — Grieg plays Wedding Day (1903) — Description, upload date, duration, source “pd” and licensing. No earlier transfer source is named.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Maureen Buja — Silver Memories: Grieg’s Wedding Day at Troldhaugen — Composition date 1896; march-like opening and contrasting subdued second section. The article’s erroneous Book I designation is not adopted.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. IMSLP — historical Grieg recording #490186 — Recording block: pianist Grieg; Paris, Gramophone & Typewriter No. 3800, 1903, matrix 2149F; recording labelled public domain.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Marston Records — Legendary Piano Recordings — Disc 1, track 8, under Paris 2 May 1903: matrix 2149F, issue 35515. Notes: early disc pitch instability; this source is discographic evidence, not the streamed transfer.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. US Copyright Office — pre-1972 sound-recording terms — Term section: recordings first published before 1923.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
